title: TLS 1.3 and QUIC handshakes

openssl.portable: OpenSSL's P-256 and X25519 assembly runs whatever OPENSSL_ia32cap says: masking every bit it reads moves a handshake by under 10% (README.md), so no mask makes a column that proves anything

rust.portable: ring picks its assembly at run time and has no feature or cfg that turns it off

node.portable: node:tls is OpenSSL's libssl with its assembly, and Node has no switch that turns it off

notes: Every QUIC column runs in memory, with no socket: Nish and Rust (quinn-proto) hand each datagram to the other endpoint, and Go runs quic-go over a pair of in-memory net.PacketConns.
Node's server sends OpenSSL's default two TLS 1.3 tickets, which node:tls cannot turn off; every other twin sends none, and nothing resumes.
